title: Etale pullback detects Zariski perfectness
statement: Let $T$ be an arbitrary scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $\epsilon_T:(T_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}})\to(T_{\mathrm{Zar}},\mathcal O_T)$ be restriction from the small etale ringed site to the Zariski ringed site [lem-trf-zariski-etale-functor-comparison-square]. Use unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and the exact tensor pullback $\epsilon_T^*$. For any $A\in D(\mathcal O_T)$, $A$ is perfect in the Zariski sense [def-pc-perfect-complex] if and only if $\epsilon_T^*A$ is perfect on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, meaning locally on that site isomorphic in the derived category to a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure modules. No quasi-coherence, boundedness, quasi-compactness or Noetherian hypothesis on $A$ or $T$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 08HG (lemma-descend-perfect), with the ringed-site perfectness convention of sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08G5 (definition-perfect).

proof.text: If $A$ is Zariski perfect, choose the open cover $T=\bigcup_iU_i$ and bounded strictly perfect representatives $P_i^\bullet$ with isomorphisms $P_i^\bullet\simeq A|_{U_i}$ in $D(\mathcal O_{U_i})$ from [def-pc-perfect-complex]. The tensor pullback $\epsilon_T^*$ is exact on all module sheaves [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence], so it is applied termwise to complexes, sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms and hence induces a functor on derived categories carrying the isomorphism $P_i^\bullet\simeq A|_{U_i}$ to an isomorphism $\epsilon^*P_i^\bullet\simeq(\epsilon_T^*A)|_{U_i}$; restriction to the etale site of the open $U_i$ commutes with $\epsilon^*$ because both are computed by tensor extension of sections over etale $V\to U_i$. For a summand $P_i^r\xrightarrow{s}\mathcal O_{U_i}^{n}\xrightarrow{t}P_i^r$ with $ts=1$, the pulled-back maps still have composite $1$, and the middle module is $\epsilon^*\mathcal O_{U_i}^{n}=\mathcal O_{U_i,\mathrm{et}}^{n}$. Bounds on degrees are unchanged. The open cover is also an etale cover, so these pulled-back strictly perfect complexes exhibit $\epsilon_T^*A$ as site-perfect.

source.place: 08HG (lemma-descend-perfect), easy direction; direct summand calculation underlying sites-cohomology.tex 08H6 (lemma-perfect-pullback).

proof.text: Conversely, suppose $\epsilon_T^*A$ is perfect. Apply the ringed-site criterion to $(T_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}})$: $\epsilon_T^*A$ is pseudo-coherent and locally has finite Tor dimension, with the interval allowed to vary on the cover.

For each integer $m$, pseudo-coherence of $\epsilon_T^*A$ gives $m$-pseudo-coherence, which descends to $A$ by the pseudo-coherence descent statement. Quantifying over $m$ proves that $A$ is pseudo-coherent. The local finite-Tor clause of Tor-dimension descent gives Zariski-locally finite Tor dimension for $A$. Both descent statements allow arbitrary $A$ and arbitrary $T$; no global bound is inferred.

Apply the scheme perfectness criterion to the pseudo-coherent object $A$ with Zariski-locally finite Tor dimension obtained in step 3. It gives precisely Zariski perfectness in [def-pc-perfect-complex], completing the converse.
